historicalReference.use: Family/unit crosswalk only; candidate UI is not evidence of implementation.

scope.semanticCoverageClaim: This is an independently audited named semantic contract, not proof of every possible code path or runtime journey. All runtime acceptance remains unperformed until evaluator evidence exists.

evaluationRules.mustKeepScoring: Score each listed input/action/result independently. A feature passes only if applicable semantics survive and an actual task outcome is observed. Catalog presence is a separate discovery metric.
noSubstitution: A toast is not a persisted result.
A route is not a working feature.
An import name is not explanatory metadata.
A generic JSON advanced editor is not an adequate substitute for each named user input.
An all-green fixture is not recovery coverage.
A server folder field is a forbidden responsibility even if it works.
evaluationRules.disclosure: Progressive disclosure is acceptable when a task-relevant labeled entry leads to all required controls before their decision point, current state is visible, and closing does not discard unacknowledged work.
evaluationRules.runtimeBoundary: Static prototypes must label backend actions as simulations and retain honest outcome/recovery states; they cannot claim production server/native validation.

evaluationApplicability.platformsMeaning: The platforms field records where implementation evidence was audited. It is not an automatic candidate-platform exemption.
evaluationApplicability.centralSharedWorkspaces: Each UF-* semantic applies on Web, Mac and Android wherever a candidate exposes that Central task, including shared Library, Import, Ask, Activity, Sources and Settings pages. A rendered import form on any platform must preserve import-context inputs, persistence and recovery.
evaluationApplicability.handoff: Where native code delegates a Central capability, an explicit functional Central handoff is acceptable; preserve the intended task and disclose the destination. A local-looking unsupported form cannot claim native implementation.
evaluationApplicability.nativeOnly: NAT-* features apply only to their listed native platforms. Use current-code distinctions for page modes, coding collection, local source-description conflicts, permissions and attachment handoffs.
evaluationApplicability.notApplicableRule: N/A requires a source-backed platform/capability reason and an honest supported handoff if the task is otherwise in scope. The central-web label alone never exempts a shared Central workspace rendered in Mac/Android candidates.

nativeAuditLimitations: This is an explicit semantic surface inventory, not a claim of all behavior under every state combination.
Some source anchors cover a grouped control; evaluation should check every enumerated input/action/result, not award credit for a single matching label.

Desktop source description field is absent from current local sourceOptions UI; Android freeform description and context conflict workflow are implemented. Do not invent Mac parity as existing behavior.
Android current quick-note UI passes empty mood despite legacy help text saying mood max80; do not claim an editable native mood field.
Android page extraction exposes two modes; Mac exposes four. Android coding-agent local collection is absent.
Central local-server directory sync is excluded by user correction; directory collection belongs on Mac/Android only.
Central processing, source context details and attribution schemas must be audited by parent against server/web code.
